# Kyoto Spring Trip Snapshot

A relaxed 4-day Kyoto plan for 2 adults, centered on temples, traditional food, and one easy day trip. The budget below keeps the trip at **about USD 1,800 total excluding flights** with a comfortable mid-range pace.

# 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget

## Day 1 — Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and take a slow walk through **Gion** and **Higashiyama**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** and nearby temple lanes at an unhurried pace.
- Evening: Traditional dinner in Higashiyama or Gion; keep the night light and early.

Estimated daily cost for 2:
- Lodging: **USD 180**
- Food: **USD 90**
- Local transport: **USD 15**
- Admissions/snacks: **USD 25**
- Day total: **USD 310**

## Day 2 — Arashiyama and Zen Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head to **Arashiyama** early for the bamboo grove and river area.
- Afternoon: Choose one major temple stop: **Tenryu-ji** or **Okochi Sanso** for a slower, scenic visit.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for kaiseki-style or set-menu Japanese dinner.

Estimated daily cost for 2:
- Lodging: **USD 180**
- Food: **USD 100**
- Local transport: **USD 20**
- Admissions/snacks: **USD 35**
- Day total: **USD 335**

## Day 3 — Nara Day Trip
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Take an easy train day trip to **Nara**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Todai-ji** and **Nara Park**; keep the pace relaxed and avoid overpacking the day.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/25/DeerNaraJapan.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Todai-ji** and **Nara Park**; keep the pace relaxed and avoid overpacking the day, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Return to Kyoto for a casual dinner near your hotel.

Estimated daily cost for 2:
- Lodging: **USD 180**
- Food: **USD 95**
- Train/local transport: **USD 35**
- Admissions/snacks: **USD 30**
- Day total: **USD 340**

## Day 4 — Northern Kyoto and Departure Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** or **Ryoan-ji**; pick one to keep the day calm.
- Afternoon: Enjoy a final lunch of tofu, soba, or yudofu, then shop for small souvenirs.
- Evening: Depart or enjoy one last easy dinner if your flight is later.

Estimated daily cost for 2:
- Lodging: **USD 180**
- Food: **USD 90**
- Local transport: **USD 20**
- Admissions/snacks: **USD 25**
- Day total: **USD 315**

## Best Neighborhoods to Stay In Kyoto

| Neighborhood | Best for | Why it works | Typical fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gion / Higashiyama | Temple access, atmosphere, food | Walkable to Kiyomizu-dera, Yasaka Shrine, traditional streets | Best overall for this trip |
| Kawaramachi / Downtown | Dining, transit, convenience | Easy buses/trains, many restaurants, good value options | Best for flexibility |
| Kyoto Station Area | Easy arrivals/departures | Simple logistics, many hotels, strong transport links | Best if you want convenience |
| Arashiyama | Scenic stays, quieter pace | Great for early temple visits and river scenery | Best if you want a slower, scenic base |

## Budget Plan for the Full Trip

- Lodging: **USD 720**
- Food: **USD 375**
- Local transport: **USD 90**
- Admissions/snacks: **USD 115**
- Buffer for tea, souvenirs, extra dessert, or taxi rides: **USD 200**
- Total planned spend: **USD 1,500**

This leaves about **USD 300** under your cap for upgrades such as a nicer ryokan night, a special kaiseki dinner, or extra shopping.

## Relaxed Trip Notes

- Keep to **1–2 major activities per day** and avoid stacking too many temples in one afternoon.
- For the most comfortable flow, do **early temple visits** and **longer meals later in the day**.
Media: Alt=For the most comfortable flow, do **early temple visits** and **longer meals later in the day**, Kyoto, Japan
- If you want one splurge, put it on **one traditional dinner** or **one ryokan-style stay** rather than spreading it across the whole trip.
